questions.question: Which of the following ancient Indian kingdoms was known for its sophisticated system of administration and architecture?
questions.explanation: The Mauryan Empire is known for its sophisticated system of administration, including a well-organized bureaucracy and a robust system of taxation, as well as its impressive architectural achievements, such as the construction of the Ashoka Pillars.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Bahmani Kingdom in the Deccan region of India?
questions.explanation: Alauddin Bahman Shah was the founder of the Bahmani Kingdom in 1347 CE, which played a significant role in the medieval history of India, particularly in the Deccan region.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume, a British civil servant, with the objective of promoting Indian rights and interests, and it later became a major force in the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in which year?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 as a protest against the Rowlatt Act and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, aiming to achieve swaraj through non-violent means.

questions.question: The ancient Indian university of Nalanda was located in which modern-day state?
questions.explanation: The ancient Indian university of Nalanda was located in present-day Bihar, and it was a major center of learning and intellectual inquiry in ancient India, attracting students and scholars from across the world.

questions.question: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by which brothers?
options: Krishnadeva Raya and Aliya Rama Raya
Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughlaq
questions.explanation: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by the brothers Harihara and Bukka Raya in the 14th century CE, and it played a significant role in the medieval history of southern India.

questions.question: The Indian Rebellion of 1857 was led by which of the following leaders?
questions.explanation: The Indian Rebellion of 1857 was a widespread uprising against British rule in India, led by various leaders including Mangal Pandey, Rani Lakshmibai, and Tantia Tope, among others.

questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in which year?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1942, with the slogan 'Do or Die', demanding immediate independence for India from British rule.

questions.question: The ancient Indian text of the Arthashastra was written by which of the following authors?
questions.explanation: The ancient Indian text of the Arthashastra was written by Kautilya, also known as Chanakya, who was a prominent advisor to the Mauryan emperor Chandragupta Maurya and is considered one of the greatest thinkers in Indian history.

questions.question: The Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti was buried in which of the following cities?
questions.explanation: The Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti was buried in Ajmer, where his dargah (tomb) is still a major pilgrimage site, attracting millions of devotees from across the world.

questions.question: What is the largest state in India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is the largest state in India by area, covering approximately 342,239 square kilometers.

questions.question: Which mountain range runs along the eastern edge of India?
questions.explanation: The Eastern Ghats mountain range runs along the eastern edge of India, parallel to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: What is the longest river in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganges is the longest river in India, stretching approximately 2,525 kilometers from its source to its delta.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major mineral resource found in India?
questions.explanation: Tin is not a major mineral resource found in India, whereas coal, iron ore, and copper are all significant mineral resources in the country.

questions.question: What type of climate does the western coastal region of India experience?
questions.explanation: The western coastal region of India experiences a tropical wet climate, characterized by high temperatures and high levels of rainfall throughout the year.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows through the states of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat?
questions.explanation: The Narmada River flows through the states of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat before emptying into the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: What is the name of the strait that separates the islands of Little Andaman and Great Nicobar?
questions.explanation: The Ten Degree Channel is the strait that separates the islands of Little Andaman and Great Nicobar in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.question: Which of the following types of soil is commonly found in the Indo-Gangetic Plain?
questions.explanation: Alluvial soil is commonly found in the Indo-Gangetic Plain, which is a fertile and densely populated region in northern India.

questions.question: What is the name of the highest peak in the Western Ghats mountain range?
questions.explanation: Anamudi is the highest peak in the Western Ghats mountain range, with an elevation of approximately 2,695 meters above sea level.

questions.question: Which of the following states has the longest coastline in India?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline in India, with a coastline of approximately 1,600 kilometers along the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Parliament of India?
options: To elect the President of India
To make laws for the country
To appoint the Prime Minister of India
To advise the Supreme Court of India
questions.explanation: The primary function of the Parliament of India is to make laws for the country.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of speech and expression?
questions.explanation: Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of speech and expression.

questions.question: What is the term of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The term of the Lok Sabha is 5 years.

questions.question: Who is the head of the Panchayati Raj system at the village level?
questions.explanation: The head of the Panchayati Raj system at the village level is the Sarpanch.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right?
questions.explanation: The Right to Property is not a Fundamental Right.

questions.question: What is the name of the advisory body that assists the President of India in the exercise of his functions?
questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers is the advisory body that assists the President of India in the exercise of his functions.

questions.question: Who has the power to appoint the Judges of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: The President of India has the power to appoint the Judges of the Supreme Court of India.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions for the protection of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
questions.explanation: Article 16 of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions for the protection of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

questions.question: What is the name of the system of governance in India at the local level?
questions.explanation: The system of governance in India at the local level is known as Panchayati Raj.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Federalism is a feature of the Indian Constitution.
